s1.syndrome_frame: Unilateral ocular findings with facial angioma and increased intraocular pressure
salient_findings: Bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve
Iris heterochromia with diffuse hyperpigmentation and micronodular elevations on the iris surface in the right eye
Increased intraocular pressure in the right eye
Diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
Increased retinal vessel tortuosity and a diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
key_facts: 12-year-old boy
Facial angioma
No leptomeningeal vascular malformations on MRI
Bilateral naevus flammeus
Visual acuity 20/20 in each eye
Iris heterochromia in the right eye
Intraocular pressure 22 mm Hg in the right eye and 12 mm Hg in the left
Open angles bilaterally
Diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye
Increased reflectance of the iris surface in the right eye on anterior-segment OCT
Increased retinal vessel tortuosity in the right eye
Diffusely darker fundus in the right eye
Choroidal thickness 2.2 mm in the right eye and 1.4 mm in the left
Early visual-field defects in the right eye
Borderline retinal nerve-fibre-layer thickness on the right

shortlist.label: Sturge-Weber syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral naevus flammeus and increased intraocular pressure in the right eye are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Glaucoma
shortlist.why_kept: Increased intraocular pressure in the right eye and early visual-field defects are indicative of glaucoma

shortlist.label: Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of naevus flammeus and ocular melanosis are consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Increased choroidal thickness and diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye are suggestive of this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Ocular melanosis
shortlist.why_kept: Iris heterochromia and diffuse trabecular hyperpigmentation in the right eye are consistent with ocular melanosis

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral naevus flammeus along the ophthalmic and maxillary divisions of the trigeminal nerve, facial angioma, and increased intraocular pressure in one eye with associated glaucomatous changes are consistent with Sturge-Weber syndrome.

rejected.label: Glaucoma
rejected.why: While glaucoma is present, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains all the key facts, such as the naevus flammeus and facial angioma.

rejected.label: Phakomatosis pigmentovascularis
rejected.why: This condition involves pigmentary and vascular abnormalities, but the specific combination of findings, including the pattern of naevus flammeus and the presence of glaucoma, is more characteristic of Sturge-Weber syndrome.

rejected.label: Diffuse choroidal hemangioma
rejected.why: The increased choroidal thickness and other ocular findings could be consistent with a choroidal hemangioma, but this diagnosis does not explain the naevus flammeus or the facial angioma.

rejected.label: Ocular melanosis
rejected.why: Ocular melanosis could explain some of the ocular findings, such as the iris heterochromia and diffuse hyperpigmentation, but it does not account for the naevus flammeus, facial angioma, or the specific pattern of glaucomatous changes.
